_about: Tables for world/ATMOSPHERE.md: the baseline air, pressure with altitude, local modifiers, the regions that become active, and the period's gas scenarios. Proposed (Rex's go-ahead via ChatGPT's compromise, 2026-10-29); numbers placeholders where marked. mark: rex | proposed | open.

altitude.title: Pressure with altitude (the standard atmosphere) and what the lungs see
altitude.source: Barometric formula P(h) = 101325 x (1 - 0.0065 h / 288.15)^5.256 for the lower atmosphere under standard conditions; oxygen stays 20.95% while total pressure falls; inspired PO2 = 0.2095 x (P - 47 mmHg). Alveolar gas equation PAO2 = FiO2 (Patm - 47) - PaCO2 / 0.8 (standard respiratory physiology; ATM-ALV). Caribbean use is small (the Blue Mountains 2,256 m); the table exists for the reusable engine.

scenarios.title: The period's gases: what a 1650 to 1730 crew actually breathed (the payoff list)
scenarios.source: Gun decks produced clouds of hazardous smoke (naval artillery overviews); black powder's gases are CO2, N2, CO, H2S, H2 and CH4 (about 43% of the products by mass; ATM-BP); stinkpots of sulphur and powder are attested from 1669 (Sturmy's Mariner's Magazine) and used by pirates and in boarding (ATM-STINK); charcoal in enclosed spaces kills by carbon monoxide (modern series: 83 US deaths in seven years from charcoal indoors; ATM-CO); below-decks air in 1741 was foul enough to be a navy complaint (ATM-VENT); volcanic islands (Montserrat, Guadeloupe, Martinique, St Vincent) have fumaroles. The hold's foul air is documented in the 19th century; the period's own deaths from it are open.
